title: Truthiness, short-circuiting, and safe conditions
sources: Python documentation: boolean operations and comparisons
masterChecklist: Comparisons, truthiness, short-circuit logic, chained comparisons, is versus ==
Conditional flow: if, elif, else, match/case, guards and structural pattern matching
Defensive conditions, validation order, readable Boolean expressions and edge cases
whyItMatters: Conditions decide whether a program proceeds, rejects input, or performs a risky action. A small mistake in truthiness or evaluation order can turn missing data into a crash or let invalid data reach later code.
simpleExplanation: In a condition, values such as False, None, zero, empty text, and empty collections are falsey; many other values are truthy. and stops as soon as its left side is falsey. or stops as soon as its left side is truthy. This short-circuit behavior lets you check that a value exists before asking for an attribute or index on it.
mentalModel: A condition is a building entrance check. and means every required check must pass, so the guard stops at the first failed check. or means any acceptable route can pass, so the guard stops once one route is valid.
outcomes: Use parentheses or named Boolean variables when a condition becomes hard to read.

realWorldExample.scenario: A study tool optionally receives a note and should count it only when it is non-empty text.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: Calling note.strip() before checking that note is text can raise an exception for None or another value. A compact but unreadable condition can hide a policy mistake.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Check type and presence in a readable order, store a meaningful Boolean when the rule has a name, and test None, empty text, whitespace, and normal text.

explanation: isinstance runs first. When note is None, and short-circuits and note.strip is never called.
For a string, strip removes outer whitespace before bool checks whether anything remains.
The function returns False for missing/blank input and True for meaningful text.
This explicit type policy is clearer than relying on every possible truthy object behaving like a note.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Pass 0 and [] to confirm that the type check makes the function reject values that are not text.

procedure: State the valid input type and the rule for empty values.
Put the safest, cheapest validation check first.
Use and to require multiple conditions and or for documented alternatives.
Name a complex decision in a Boolean variable instead of nesting unreadable expressions.
Test missing, empty, boundary, and normal inputs.

commonMistakes.mistake: Calling a method before checking the value exists or has the right type.
commonMistakes.why: None or a wrong type can raise before the condition can safely reject it.
commonMistakes.avoid: Order conditions so a safe validation check short-circuits first.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using an empty string or zero as a universal missing-value test.
commonMistakes.why: Zero can be a valid numeric value and empty text can be an intentional value depending on the domain.
commonMistakes.avoid: Define the domain rule explicitly and use is None when you mean the None sentinel.

commonMistakes.mistake: Writing one long Boolean expression with unclear precedence.
commonMistakes.why: Readers can misunderstand the policy and alter it incorrectly.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use parentheses or named intermediate Booleans.

lab.title: Accept only meaningful fictional study notes
lab.safety: Uses only local values in memory.
guidedSteps: Strip whitespace only after the type check can pass.
Wrap the stripped text in bool.
Test None, whitespace, and normal text.
Explain why None does not call strip.
checks: Returns False for None and blank text.
Returns True for a non-blank string.
Does not catch an exception to hide a validation-order bug.
lab.solutionExplanation: The type test runs first. If it is false, and returns immediately, so blank or missing values are rejected without calling a string method on an invalid value.
challenges: Find the bug: call note.strip() before isinstance(note, str).
Experiment: decide whether a note made only of a newline should count and test your chosen rule.

projectConnection.milestone: Validate optional note fields with documented missing/blank rules before saving a plan.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: The editor does not crash on None or whitespace-only notes and has tests showing the intended decision for each input category.

assessment.question: What does and do when its left side is falsey?
assessment.answer: It stops evaluating and returns without evaluating the right side.

assessment.question: Why is isinstance(note, str) placed first?
assessment.answer: It prevents note.strip() from being called on None or another non-string value.

assessment.question: Should zero always mean missing data?
assessment.answer: No. Zero may be a valid domain value.
